parts.text: A student is determining the refractive index n of the material of a transparent block. Fig. 3.1 shows the outline ABCD of the block.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) • On Fig. 3.1, draw a normal NL at the centre of side AB . • Continue the normal so that it passes through side CD of the block. [1]

ms.label: 3(a)(i)
ms.text: normal at centre of AB (by eye) produced to cross CD

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) • Label the point F where NL crosses AB . • Label the point G where NL crosses CD . • Draw a line EF at an angle i = 30° to the left of the normal and above side AB . [1]

ms.label: 3(a)(ii)
ms.text: i = 30° ± 1° drawn to the left of the normal

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Mark the positions of two pins P 1 and P 2 on line EF placed at a suitable distance apart for this type of ray-tracing experiment. [1]

ms.label: 3(a)(iii)
ms.text:
P and P in air at minimum distance apart of 5.0cm
1
2

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student observes the images of P 1 and P 2 through side CD of the block. He places two pins P 3 and P 4 between his eye and the block so that P 3 , P 4 and the images of P 1 and P 2 seen through the block, all appear exactly one behind the other. The positions of P 3 and P 4 are marked on Fig. 3.1. • Draw a line passing through P 3 and P 4 . Continue the line until it meets the normal NL . • Label the point J where the line meets the normal. • Label the point H where the line meets side CD . Draw the line FH . [1]

ms.label: 3(b)
ms.text:
line through P and P neat, straight and continued to N

ms.text: b = 37 ± 1 mm and both with correct unit

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the refractive index n using the equation n = a b . n = ........................................................... [2]

ms.label: 3(c)(iii)
ms.text:

ms.text:
